title: Electric sweeping between tram tracks: HTM shares its first experiences with the eCleango 550
body_markdown:
### From diesel to electric


When its existing diesel-powered sweepers were due for replacement, HTM deliberately looked for an electric alternative. Whenever a vehicle needs to be replaced, the organisation assesses whether electrification is a viable option.


The Schmidt eCleango 550 was selected following a European tender process, in which Aebi Schmidt was able to meet all the specified requirements. With this investment, HTM takes another step towards electrifying its vehicle fleet.


### Keeping tram tracks and depots clean


The two machines are used for a variety of cleaning tasks. They keep the depot areas clean, where trams and buses are parked and depart for their daily services.


They also clean dedicated tramways: sections of track that are accessible only to trams and, where permitted, emergency vehicles.


These areas include switches and tram tracks embedded in asphalt or road paving. By regularly removing dirt, leaves and other debris, the tracks and switches are kept clean. This contributes to safe and smooth tram operations and is therefore an important part of maintaining this infrastructure.


### Greater comfort for operators


The transition to electric equipment initially required some adjustment. While the previous machines were mainly operated using physical buttons, several functions of the eCleango 550 are controlled through a digital display.


By now, even operators who had worked with diesel-powered machines for many years have become familiar with the new controls. They also report less vibration, lower noise levels and improved comfort.


The machines meet HTM's requirements for its daily cleaning operations.


### Electric operation in practice


When working with electric equipment, planning charging times is also an important consideration. Both eCleango 550 sweepers are equipped with six battery packs, the largest available configuration. The battery capacity is well suited to daily operations, and so far, HTM has not experienced any limitations in operating time.


The transition to electric equipment supports HTM in reducing local exhaust emissions during daily operations, while continuing to meet operational requirements.


By introducing these two electric sweepers, HTM continues the electrification of its vehicle fleet. This enables cleaning operations across its public transport infrastructure without local exhaust emissions from the driving and sweeping systems.
